summary: Streaming chat stalls mid-response after initial data with intermittent 502 bursts from edge proxy
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (NoteFlow) reports their streaming chat sessions for a pinned model begin sending tokens for ~5-10s then abruptly stall for 20-45s before either continuing or closing with a 502. Observed primarily from their Dedicated pool in us-east. Impact: interactive editor sessions unusable for end users (timeouts / perceived freezes).

Impact:
- Multiple users reporting freezing editor while generation appears to hang mid-sentence.
- Customer seeing surge of HTTP 502s reported in their client telemetry coincident with stalls.

Environment:
- Dedicated cluster id: ded-88-us-east
- API endpoint: api.redwood-inference.com (prod, us-east)
steps_to_reproduce: Open streaming chat session against NoteFlow account with model redwood-13b-v2 pinned
Send prompt that triggers ~800-1200 token output (e.g., long summarization)
Observe tokens stream for 5-12s then stall; client heartbeat continues but no new chunks; sometimes connection ends with 502
Reproduce under burst load by sending 5 parallel sessions from single IP
logs_and_traces: Datadog traces: trace_id=abc123: shows initial request routed to proxy-edge-02 -> serving-worker-7; last span before quiet is proxy:write-chunk
nginx/error.log on proxy-edge-02: 'upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream' timestamps align with stalls
Serving runtime worker logs: 'kv-cache miss; continuing generation' then no further log lines for 30s
Customer client shows HTTP/1.1 502 responses on reconnect after stall
timeline: 2026-03-10 09:12 UTC - Customer first opened ticket to support with sample logs
2026-03-10 09:33 UTC - Support reproduced issue in internal staging with small probability
2026-03-10 12:00 UTC - Escalated to SRE and serving-runtime oncall
2026-03-11 03:10 UTC - Noted correlated burst of 502s across other dedicated pools for different customers; created INC-2026
2026-03-12 18:40 UTC - Experimented with proxy keepalive tuning and observed reduction in 502 frequency but stalls still occur
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: edge proxy (streaming-proxy/nginx layer) intermittently closing upstream while kernel-level TCP retransmits delay chunk delivery; observed repeated 'upstream prematurely closed connection' messages. Secondary hypothesis: serving-runtime worker enters brief CPU stall when processing large KV-cache eviction under quantized models leading to no flush of chunked responses.

What we tried so far:
- Increased proxy keepalive timeout from 30s -> 90s in a canary pool (reduced abrupt closes but not full elimination).
- Forced fallback from persistent connection to chunked encoding variation (no change).
- Replayed customer payloads against dedicated workers with debug logging; saw long GC-like pauses at worker process level in 6% of runs.
- Correlated Datadog CPU and cgroup throttling metrics: small spikes on host with worker causing delayed write() to proxy socket.

Open leads:
- Kernel-level TCP retransmit/backoff during rekey (we saw two TLS rekey events on host at timestamps that match stalls). Need network team to confirm if ipsec/VPC maintenance coincided.
- Possible interaction between proxy buffering and nginx 1.20 chunked flush heuristics; upstream code path may be deferring flush when write buffer below threshold during CPU pause.

Related artifacts:
- Slack thread: #support (https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C05N2H7Q9)
- Datadog dashboard: https://app.datadoghq.com/dashboard/streaming/stalls-us-east

comments: Aisha Patel (Support) 2026-03-10: Customer reports ~30% of long generations stall; attached client HAR and server timestamps
Marcus Chen (SRE) 2026-03-10: Reproduced locally with probabilty ~6%. Observed upstream closed messages on proxy-edge-02. I've collected core dumps and enabled debug on proxy.

Lena Ortiz (Serving Runtime Eng) 2026-03-11: I see sporadic GC-like pauses in the worker logs when running quantized model path; adding additional logging around evictions and serialization to confirm
Aisha Patel (Support) 2026-03-12: Customer accepted temporary mitigation of reducing max-generation length to 600 tokens; reports reduction in frequency but still hit in heavy loops
Marcus Chen (SRE) 2026-03-13: Scheduled kernel/TLS rekey audit with Networking team for 2026-03-14 02:00 UTC; will coordinate to check for rekey events correlating with stalls
mitigation_and_workarounds: Temporary workaround provided to customer: pin model to a smaller-generation config (< 600 tokens) and enable client-side reconnect/backfill logic. We rolled canary proxy keepalive change to customer's dedicated pool which reduced 502 reconnects by ~60%. Recommended customer to enable incremental flushing in client so partial outputs are persisted.
next_steps: 1) Networking to confirm whether ipsec/TLS rekeying events align with stall timestamps (assigned to Network Ops). 2) Serving Runtime team to add preemptible flush on worker when eviction/GC predicted: instrument and deploy small patch in canary pool (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/334). 3) Proxy team to evaluate nginx chunked flush parameters and add healthcheck for upstream socket pauses. 4) Monitor canary for 72h and collect additional traces; update customer after 48h.
